newsitem.title: USA: Hayes to acquire Cardinal Technologies - source.
newsitem.headline: Hayes to acquire Cardinal Technologies - source.

text.p: Hayes Microcomputer Products Inc is expected to announce shortly the acquisition of another modem maker, Cardinal Technologies Inc, an executive close to the deal said on Thursday.
Terms of the merger will not be disclosed as both companies are private, the source said.
Officials of the two companies were not immediately available to comment on the anticipated deal.
Hayes is based in Atlanta. Cardinal is headquartered in St. Louis.
Microsoft Corp co-founder Paul Allen holds majority control in Cardinal Technologies.
Later, Jim Jonez, Cardinal's director of product marketing, confirmed the outlines of the deal.
The Cardinal official said Hayes and Cardinal have signed a letter of intent to merge. Secondly, Allen's Vulcan Ventures Inc has agreed to take a stake in Hayes Microcomputer, he said.
Further financial terms were not disclosed in either deal. The merger is expected to close later this month, Jonez said.
"Hayes and Cardinal have signed a letter of intent. In a seperate transaction, Vulcan Ventures will become an investor in Hayes," Jonez said.

Hayes, which invented the modern personal computer modem standard and dominated the industry in its first decade, lost ground to low-cost clone makers in the late 1980s. It underwent a Chapter 11 bankruptcy in 1994.
The company now ranks as the second largest consumer modem maker after U.S. Robotics Corp. Hayes also sells software and a range of Wide Area Networking (WAN) equipment.
Founder Dennis Hayes reportedly owns a majority of his company's stock.
Cardinal's principal products are consumer modems targetted at the small office/home office market. They are distributed through retail outlets and by direct mail order, Jonez said.
